literature_notes: CDH1 (E-cadherin) is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein: signal peptide residues 1–22 are cleaved, the ectodomain spans residues 23–709, the TM helix spans 710–730, and the cytoplasmic tail spans 731–882. All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe C-terminal tags — an endogenous CRISPR/Cas9 HA knock-in (L1, L3) and a pEGFPN3 GFP fusion (L2). Because the CDH1 C-terminus (residue 882) is intracellular, every one of these tags is cytoplasmic. None of the ledger lines describes a tag at the mature N-terminus (after residue 22), in any extracellular loop, or anywhere else on the ectodomain. No ledger line qualifies as evidence for an extracellular surface tag site; therefore sites = [].

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag knocked into the native CDH1 locus via CRISPR/Cas9 in BG1 cells; the CDH1 C-terminus is intracellular (residues 731–882), so this tag is cytoplasmic and cannot serve as a surface epitope.
Full-length Cdh1 C-terminally fused to GFP via pEGFPN3; the C-terminus is intracellular, making this an intracellular fluorescent fusion, not a surface tag.
